(Applications No.85068 and 85066 - both of 2019)
1. Application No.85068 of 2019 seeks recall of order dated 8.9.2014.
Since the application has been filed after considerable delay, application No.85066 of 2019 has been filed for condonation of the delay.

2. Learned counsel for the State Mr. Raj Baksh Singh has very fairly stated that in view of the nature of the issue, he would have no objection if order dated 8.9.2014 is recalled, and the main petition is heard today itself.

Counsel for Petitioner :- Farooq Ayub Counsel for Respondent :- C.S.C.,B.L.Verma,Virendra Kumar Shukla Hon'ble Ajai Lamba,J.
Hon'ble Narendra Kumar Johari,J.
(Oral)

1. The petition seeks issuance of a writ in the nature of mandamus directing respondent No.4 (Station House Officer, P.S. Kotwali, district Barabanki) not to create hindrance in functioning and carrying business of the petitioners of slaughtering and selling buffaloes' meat in village Alapur, P.S.
Kotwali, district Barabanki.

2. We have taken notice of the fact that when the case came up for hearing on 29.8.2008, the following order was passed :
"Notice on behalf of opposite parties 1 to 4 has been accepted by learned Chief Standing Counsel.
Notice on behalf of respondent no.5 has been accepted by Sri Virendra Kumar Shukla.

In the meantime, it is provided that in case no bye laws has been framed by the Zila Panchayat and there are no statutory rules or valid executive orders for restraining the petitioners for slaughtering and selling the buffalo's meat at the particular place,
the petitioners' business shall not be interfered with. "
3.

Learned counsel for the petitioners has pointed out that there has been a development in so much as the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 provides for making application for grant of licence for slaughtering the buffaloes and selling its meat.
Learned counsel contends that in the further development, the petitioners applied for licence on 25.4.2017.
However, neither licence has been granted nor the petitioners are being allowed to pursue their profession.

Hazi Hasan & 2 Ors. vs State Of U.P. Thru Secy. Home & 4 Ors. on 2 August, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119669257/
2 4.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the State Mr. Raj Baksh Singh, however, has pointed out that a new Act, viz Food Safety and Standards (Amendment) Act, 2017 has come into force.
The petitioners are required to make an application under the provisions of the Amendment Act of 2017.

The Court has been further assured that in case an application for grant of licence is filed under the Food Safety and Standards (Amendment) Act, 2017, decision thereon would be taken within a period of four weeks of making the application.
5.
In view of the assurance given by learned counsel for the State Mr. Raj Baksh Singh, this petition is disposed of.
The petitioners would be at liberty to file an application under the Amendment Act of 2017(supra), which would be dealt with in accordance with law within four weeks.
